title: Non-invasive blood pressure measurement with ClearSight during interhospital intensive care transfers: Comparison with arterial reference measurement
summary:
This study investigates how reliably a modern, non-invasive blood pressure measurement system (ClearSight system) measures blood pressure during interhospital transport between two hospitals (intensive care units). Normally, the blood pressure of critically ill patients is measured directly in an artery via a thin catheter - this is very accurate, but also invasive.

The ClearSight system measures blood pressure continuously via a sensor on the finger without the need to insert a catheter. In the study, both systems - the established arterial method and the new ClearSight system - will be used simultaneously during transport. This will make it possible to check how well the values of the non-invasive system match the reference values under real conditions (e.g. vibrations, movement).

The aim is to evaluate the accuracy and reliability of the ClearSight system during the transport of critically ill patients - and thus to test its potential role as a supplement or alternative to invasive measurement.
